subject: maths
title: Primary 5 Multiplying Fractions
seo_title: P5 Multiplying Fractions Worksheets: Free Primary 5 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Multiplying a proper/improper fraction and a whole number, a proper fraction and a proper/improper fraction, two improper fractions, and a mixed number and a whole number
meta_desc: Free P5 maths practice: multiply fractions by whole numbers, fractions and mixed numbers, with area and bar models. 100 questions with answers (MOE syllabus).
key_big: Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators. A whole number multiplies only the numerator.
body_html:
The big idea

To multiply fractions, multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators. A whole number has no denominator to multiply: write 12 as 121, so only the numerator changes. Give answers in simplest form, and change improper fractions to mixed numbers.

Fraction × whole number

34 × 12 means 34 of 12. Draw a model and use units.

Example 1

25 × 3 = ?

Multiply the numerator: 2 × 3 = 6, and keep the denominator 5. 65 = 1 15.

Answer: 1 15

Fraction × fraction

“Of” means ×. The area model shows 23 of 34.

Example 2

94 × 83 = ?

Simplify first: divide 9 and 3 by 3, and divide 8 and 4 by 4. Now 3 × 2 = 6. Always pair a numerator with a denominator.

Answer: 6

Mixed number × whole number

Change the mixed number to an improper fraction first. Then multiply.

Example 3

2 34 × 3 = ?

2 34 = 114 (2 × 4 + 3 = 11). 114 × 3 = 334 = 8 14.

Answer: 8 14

Word problems: a fraction of the remainder

Draw the whole, then cut the remainder into equal units. Count the units, find 1 unit, then the answer.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
34 × 12 = 348 (multiplying the whole number into the denominator)Multiply the numerator: 364 = 9
25 × 3 = 3 25 (adding instead of multiplying)3 lots of 25 = 65 = 1 15
23 × 45 = 68 (adding across)Multiply across: 815
2 34 × 3 = 6 34 (multiplying only the whole number part)114 × 3 = 8 14
Finding 14 of the whole instead of 14 of the remainderUse the remainder as the new whole in the model

faq.q: What is taught in P5 multiplying fractions?
faq.a: Primary 5 students multiply a fraction by a whole number, a proper fraction by a proper or improper fraction, two improper fractions, and a mixed number by a whole number, without a calculator. They also solve word problems such as finding a fraction of a remainder.

faq.q: How do I explain multiplying fractions to my child?
faq.a: Start with “of”: 2/3 × 3/4 means 2/3 of 3/4, and an area model shows 6 of 12 parts, which is 1/2. Then show the rule: multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Multiplying the whole number into the denominator, such as 3/4 × 12 = 3/48. The whole number multiplies only the numerator, so 3/4 × 12 = 36/4 = 9. Another is multiplying only the whole number part of a mixed number.

faq.q: Is multiplying fractions in the MOE syllabus for Primary 5?
faq.a: Yes. It is part of Fractions in the MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus for Primary 5. Fraction word problems like these also appear in Primary 6 and the PSLE.

items.q: The model shows 34 × 12. What is 34 × 12?
items.e: 34 × 12 means 34 of 12. 4 units = 12, so 1 unit = 12 ÷ 4 = 3. 3 units = 3 × 3 = 9.

items.q: The model shows 23 × 15. What is 23 × 15?
items.e: 23 × 15 means 23 of 15. 3 units = 15, so 1 unit = 15 ÷ 3 = 5. 2 units = 2 × 5 = 10.

items.q: The model shows 45 × 20. What is 45 × 20?
items.e: 45 × 20 means 45 of 20. 5 units = 20, so 1 unit = 20 ÷ 5 = 4. 4 units = 4 × 4 = 16.

items.q: The model shows 56 × 18. What is 56 × 18?
items.e: 56 × 18 means 56 of 18. 6 units = 18, so 1 unit = 18 ÷ 6 = 3. 5 units = 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: The model shows 38 × 24. What is 38 × 24?
items.e: 38 × 24 means 38 of 24. 8 units = 24, so 1 unit = 24 ÷ 8 = 3. 3 units = 3 × 3 = 9.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 3 bars with 25 shaded in each. What is 25 × 3?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 3 × 2 = 6 fifths. So 25 × 3 = 65 = 1 15.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 4 bars with 34 shaded in each. What is 34 × 4?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 4 × 3 = 12 quarters. So 34 × 4 = 124 = 3.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 5 bars with 23 shaded in each. What is 23 × 5?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 5 × 2 = 10 thirds. So 23 × 5 = 103 = 3 13.

items.q: Raju says 34 × 12 = 348. What mistake did he make?
c: He forgot to simplify the answer.
He multiplied the denominator by 12 instead of the numerator.
items.e: 348 is smaller than 34, but 12 lots of 34 must be more. Multiply the numerator: 34 × 12 = 364 = 9. He multiplied the denominator by 12 instead of the numerator.

items.q: The model shows 23 of 34. What fraction of the whole square is dark green? Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The square is cut into 4 × 3 = 12 equal parts, and 3 × 2 = 6 of them are dark green. So 23 × 34 = 612 = 12.

items.q: The model shows 12 of 35. What fraction of the whole square is dark green? Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The square is cut into 5 × 2 = 10 equal parts, and 3 × 1 = 3 of them are dark green. So 12 × 35 = 310.

items.q: The model shows 34 of 25. What fraction of the whole square is dark green? Give your answer in its simplest form.

items.q: The model shows 23 of 14. What fraction of the whole square is dark green? Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The square is cut into 4 × 3 = 12 equal parts, and 1 × 2 = 2 of them are dark green. So 23 × 14 = 212 = 16.

items.q: The light green columns are 23 of the square. Which multiplication does the dark green part show?
c: 35 × 23
25 × 23
35 × 13
35 + 23
items.e: The dark green part is 3 of the 5 rows inside the light green columns, so it is 35 of 23: 35 × 23.

items.q: 34 × 23 = 12. Which sentence is true?
c: The answer is smaller than both fractions.
The answer is greater than both fractions.
The answer is equal to one of the fractions.
The answer is between the two fractions.
items.e: 12 is less than 34 and less than 23. Taking a part of a part gives a smaller amount, so the answer is smaller than both fractions.

items.q: Which multiplication can be simplified before multiplying?
c: 49 × 35
58 × 37
34 × 57
25 × 37
items.e: Look for a numerator and a denominator with a common factor. In 49 × 35, 3 and 9 share 3: 49 × 35 = 43 × 15 = 415. The others have no such pair.

items.q: Arjun wants to simplify 635 × 149 before multiplying, so he divides 6 and 14 by 2. What is wrong?
c: Nothing is wrong. Any two numbers with a common factor can be divided.
You can never simplify before multiplying.
6 and 14 are both numerators. Pair a numerator with a denominator.
items.e: Dividing two numerators changes the value. Pair a numerator with a denominator: 6 and 9 share 3, and 14 and 35 share 7. Then 25 × 23 = 415. 6 and 14 are both numerators. Pair a numerator with a denominator.

items.q: Without calculating, which product is greater than 54?
c: 54 × 12
54 × 67
54 × 76
54 × 33
items.e: Multiplying by a number greater than 1 gives a greater answer. 76 is greater than 1, so 54 × 76 is greater than 54. 33 = 1, and 67 and 12 are less than 1.

items.q: Each row shows 2 14. There are 3 rows. What is 2 14 × 3?
items.e: Count the whole bars: 3 × 2 = 6. Count the shaded quarters in the last column: 3 × 1 = 3. Change 2 14 to an improper fraction: 2 × 4 + 1 = 9, so 2 14 = 94. Then 94 × 3 = 9 × 34 = 274 = 6 34.

items.q: Each row shows 1 25. There are 2 rows. What is 1 25 × 2?
items.e: Count the whole bars: 2 × 1 = 2. Count the shaded fifths in the last column: 2 × 2 = 4. Change 1 25 to an improper fraction: 1 × 5 + 2 = 7, so 1 25 = 75. Then 75 × 2 = 7 × 25 = 145 = 2 45.

items.q: Each row shows 1 13. There are 4 rows. What is 1 13 × 4?
items.e: Count the whole bars: 4 × 1 = 4. Count the shaded thirds in the last column: 4 × 1 = 4. Change 1 13 to an improper fraction: 1 × 3 + 1 = 4, so 1 13 = 43. Then 43 × 4 = 4 × 43 = 163 = 5 13.

items.q: Each row shows 2 34. There are 3 rows. What is 2 34 × 3?
items.e: Count the whole bars: 3 × 2 = 6. Count the shaded quarters in the last column: 3 × 3 = 9. Change 2 34 to an improper fraction: 2 × 4 + 3 = 11, so 2 34 = 114. Then 114 × 3 = 11 × 34 = 334 = 8 14.

items.q: To find 2 34 × 3, first write 2 34 as an improper fraction. Which is it?
items.e: 2 wholes are 2 × 4 = 8 quarters. Add 3 more: 8 + 3 = 11. So 2 34 = 114.

items.q: To find 3 25 × 3, first write 3 25 as an improper fraction. Which is it?
items.e: 3 wholes are 3 × 5 = 15 fifths. Add 2 more: 15 + 2 = 17. So 3 25 = 175.

items.q: Ethan says 2 34 × 3 = 6 34. What mistake did he make?
c: He multiplied only the whole number part by 3.
items.e: Both parts must be multiplied: 114 × 3 = 334 = 8 14, not 6 34. He multiplied only the whole number part by 3.

items.q: Which is the same as 1 23 × 4?
items.e: 1 23 = 53 (1 × 3 + 2 = 5), so 1 23 × 4 is the same as 53 × 4 = 203 = 6 23.

items.q: A bottle holds 34 ℓ of soya bean milk. How much soya bean milk is there in 6 such bottles?
items.e: Find 6 × 34. Multiply the numerator by 6 and keep the denominator: 34 × 6 = 3 × 64 = 184 = 92 = 4 12 ℓ.

items.q: Wei Ming uses 25 m of ribbon for each gift. He wraps 7 gifts. How much ribbon does he use?
items.e: Find 7 × 25. Multiply the numerator by 7 and keep the denominator: 25 × 7 = 2 × 75 = 145 = 2 45 m.

items.q: Ahmad jogs 710 km at East Coast Park every morning. How far does he jog in 5 mornings?
items.e: Find 5 × 710. Multiply the numerator by 5 and keep the denominator: 710 × 5 = 7 × 510 = 3510 = 72 = 3 12 km.

items.q: A bag of flour has a mass of 2 14 kg. Mdm Wong buys 3 bags. What is the total mass of the flour?
items.e: Change 2 14 to an improper fraction: 2 × 4 + 1 = 9, so 2 14 = 94. Then 94 × 3 = 9 × 34 = 274 = 6 34 kg.

items.q: A durian has a mass of 1 35 kg. What is the total mass of 4 such durians?
items.e: Change 1 35 to an improper fraction: 1 × 5 + 3 = 8, so 1 35 = 85. Then 85 × 4 = 8 × 45 = 325 = 6 25 kg.

items.q: A tin holds 2 34 ℓ of paint. Mr Rahman needs 6 tins to paint the walls of his HDB flat. How much paint is that?
items.e: Change 2 34 to an improper fraction: 2 × 4 + 3 = 11, so 2 34 = 114. Then 114 × 6 = 11 × 64 = 664 = 332 = 16 12 ℓ.

items.q: There are 40 students in a Primary 5 class. 38 of them join a sports CCA. How many students join a sports CCA?
items.e: 8 units = 40, so 1 unit = 40 ÷ 8 = 5. 3 units = 3 × 5 = 15 students.

items.q: Kumar had $60. He spent 25 of it on a storybook. How much money did he have left?
items.e: 5 units = $60, so 1 unit = $60 ÷ 5 = $12. He spent 2 units, so 3 units are left: 3 × $12 = $36.

items.q: Mei Ling had a ribbon 34 m long. She used 23 of it to tie a bow. What length of ribbon did she use?
items.e: 23 of 34 m is 23 × 34. Simplify first: divide 2 and 4 by 2, and the 3s cancel. Now 1 × 12 = 12 m.

items.q:
Mr Tan planted vegetables on 45 of his garden. Chilli plants cover 12 of the vegetable part. What fraction of the whole garden is covered by chilli plants?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: 12 of 45 is 12 × 45. Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators: 12 × 45 = 1 × 42 × 5 = 410 = 25.

items.q: A rectangular mat is 54 m long and 65 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 54 × 65. Simplify first: the 5s cancel, and divide 6 and 4 by 2. Now 12 × 3 = 32 = 1 12 m².

items.q: Chloe had $200. She spent 25 of it on a bag and 14 of the remainder on a book. How much did she spend on the book?
items.e: Cut the whole into 5 parts. The bag is 2 parts, and the remainder is 3 parts. Cut each part into 4 units, so the whole is 20 units and the remainder is 12 units. 14 of 12 units = 3 units. 20 units = $200, so 1 unit = $10. The book cost 3 × $10 = $30.

items.q: There are 360 students in the hall. 35 of them are girls. 14 of the girls wear spectacles. How many girls wear spectacles?
items.e: Girls: 5 units = 360, so 1 unit = 72 and 3 units = 216 girls. 14 of 216 = 216 ÷ 4 = 54. (Or 14 of 35 = 320, and 320 of 360 = 54.) So 54 girls wear spectacles.

items.q: Mrs Ng made 120 curry puffs. She sold 34 of them in the morning and 23 of the remainder in the afternoon. How many curry puffs were left?
items.e: The remainder is 14 of 120 = 30. She sold 23 of 30 = 20 in the afternoon, so 30 − 20 = 10 were left. In units: 12 units = 120, 1 unit = 10, and 1 unit is left. 10 curry puffs were left.

items.q: A fruit seller had 72 durians. He sold 58 of them on Saturday and 23 of the remainder on Sunday. How many durians did he sell on Sunday?
items.e: The remainder is 3 of the 8 units. 23 of 3 units = 2 units. 8 units = 72, so 1 unit = 9. On Sunday he sold 2 × 9 = 18 durians.

items.q: Hafiz spends 34 h on homework every day. 13 of that time is spent on maths. How many minutes does he spend on maths?
items.e: 13 × 34 = 14 h. 1 h = 60 min, so 14 h = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 min.

items.q: A shop sells cloth at $6 per metre. Mrs Lim buys 2 34 m of cloth. How much does she pay?
items.e: 2 34 × 6 = 114 × 6 = 664 = 16 12. 12 of $1 is 50¢, so she pays $16.50.

items.q: Mr Kumar buys 4 boxes of mandarin oranges for Chinese New Year. Each box has a mass of 4 12 kg. What is the total mass of the 4 boxes?
items.e: Change 4 12 to an improper fraction: 4 × 2 + 1 = 9, so 4 12 = 92. Then 92 × 4 = 9 × 42 = 362 = 18 kg.

items.q: There are 36 students in a class. 23 of them went to the Singapore Zoo. 34 of these students watched the animal feeding show. How many students watched the show?
items.e: 23 of 36 = 36 ÷ 3 × 2 = 24 students went to the zoo. 34 of 24 = 24 ÷ 4 × 3 = 18 students. (Or 34 × 23 = 12, and 12 of 36 = 18.)

items.q: Ryan gave 14 of his stickers to his brother and 13 of the remainder to his friends. He had 30 stickers left. How many stickers did he have at first?
items.e: The brother got 1 of 4 units, so the remainder is 3 units. 13 of the remainder = 1 unit went to the friends, so 2 units are left. 2 units = 30, so 1 unit = 15. At first: 4 × 15 = 60 stickers. (Do not find 13 of the whole for the friends: that gives 72.)
